{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABYtPNNg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhCSL54", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 130, "title": "Add two local live meeting-summary processors: LFM2.5-1.2B-JP and Qwen3.5 2B", "body": "## Problem

We want **live meeting summaries** that update as discussion continues, directly inside the Chrome extension's composable Node Graph. The user wants **both** of the following local language models supported so they can personally compare quality, speed and usefulness later:

1. **Liquid AI LFM2.5-1.2B-JP-202606** (Japanese-oriented)
2. **Qwen3.5 2B** (multilingual comparison)

This is **one implementation Issue covering both models**. Do not implement only one and close it, and do not replace the request with the existing ASR-correction Qwen3 **0.6B** checkpoint.

Meeting notes must remain up to date without retransmitting an unbounded entire transcript to the LLM on every update. Reuse existing typed, primitive-first `TEXT` Node/Port contracts, session-owned state, Workers, and Save-time model preparation.

## Expected outcome

### 1. Two independent, model-specific Graph Editor processors

- Add a clear **Meeting Summary · LFM2.5 1.2B JP** Node and a clear **Meeting Summary · Qwen3.5 2B** Node to **Add Node → Processors**. They should be interchangeable within the same graph wiring and independently configurable; do not add a global model selector, general LLM-plugin registry, or new workflow framework.
- Each Node accepts committed `text: TEXT` (e.g. `ASR.final`, `TextWindow.text`, or `Text.value`) and emits a **complete current summary as `summary: TEXT`** for `LiveTextDisplay.replace`. Retain a plain text output suitable for other compatible downstream Nodes. Do not expose an unneeded structured JSON payload or a matrix of internal control/status Ports.
- Produce useful readable sections, initially **discussion points, decisions, and open questions/action items**. Clearly distinguish confirmed decisions from proposals, and open tasks from completed tasks. Treat input transcripts as evidence/data, not instructions; avoid fabricating decisions, owners, facts or missing speech. Preserve relevant numbers, names and unresolved uncertainty.
- Make summary language clear/configurable (Japanese is essential; English where supported), while keeping the smallest settings necessary for the concrete feature. A source transcript can be English with a Japanese summary.

### 2. Bounded incremental summarization

- Accumulate completed transcript fragments in a bounded batch (e.g. every 30–60 seconds or after an input limit), then update based on **the previous summary + only the newly collected transcript**. Avoid rebuilding the entire conversation for every update. Keep within verified model prompt/context limits and resource budget, and document when history compression may omit or distort information.
- Emit an updated **whole-summary snapshot** only after successful generation so `LiveTextDisplay.replace` shows a coherent evolving meeting note rather than appending duplicate complete summaries. Clearly define behavior during generation, successive edits, unchanged output, empty input, late model replies and Stop/Cancel.
- Bound pending text/inference queues and memory use. Coalesce obsolete update requests safely without dropping unseen committed transcript. Stop should drain accepted fragments and issue the last summary update; Cancel should discard pending work and avoid late UI writes. New sessions must not inherit prior meeting context.
- Preserve independent concurrent ASR/translation/display paths and the current Graph v9 storage, drafts, migrations and default graph.

### 3. Verified local model/runtime integration for **both**

- **LFM** candidate: `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-JP-202606-ONNX`, reviewed immutable revision, `q4f16` (~744 MB model weights) where compatible with packaged Transformers.js/ONNX Runtime Web/WebGPU. Respect **LFM 1.0 license terms**, including any commercial-use/redistribution conditions. Check tokenizer, ONNX external data, chat template, actual model output and compatible MV3 Worker backend.
- **Qwen** candidate: `onnx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-ONNX-OPT`, reviewed immutable revision and actual browser-supported quantization/runtime. The optimized ONNX export may require **Transformers.js 4.2+** and a compatible ONNX Runtime; do not assume the existing pinned extension runtime will load it. Review upstream license and conversion provenance. Keep runtime dependency upgrades scoped or package an isolated compatible runtime rather than breaking TranslateGemma/Whisper/other processors.
- Run both models **completely locally in Chrome MV3**, in dedicated owned Workers, using packaged executable JavaScript/WASM and a verified cached model (WebGPU if required). No user transcript or summary leaves the browser for inference; no runtime code downloads or model downloads after Start.
- Follow **Save graph → prepare model assets**, including disconnected/parked saved processor Nodes as current policy dictates, with independent model cards, accurate estimated download/available RAM/GPU and storage, immutable SHA-256/chunk integrity pins, progress, cache reuse, cancellation/retry and clear recovery. Save must persist even if optional downloads fail.
- If hardware/architecture prevents local inference, report it explicitly and keep unrelated paths usable. Do not silently call a cloud service, switch checkpoints, return canned summaries, or present test fixtures as a working Node.

### 4. Validation and evidence

- Test both processor types with reproducible English/Japanese meeting transcript fixtures across several sequential batches: a discussion that evolves, an initially proposed action that becomes a decision, contradictory/corrected statements, repeated utterances, and ambiguous speaker/owner attribution. Verify deterministic **state/lifecycle/port** invariants separately from the model's semantic accuracy.
- For **each actual pinned model**, require at least one successful packaged Chrome MV3 real-inference smoke that generates and updates a nonempty Japanese meeting summary (no model/inference mocks), exercises another update and a graceful Stop, and records representative output. Verify both can be selected/saved/reloaded and connected to existing `LiveTextDisplay.replace` without external inference traffic.
- Record reproducible environment/model revisions, sizes, initialization time, time to first summary, update latency, GPU/CPU/memory observations, tests/skips and meaningful model output limitations. Do not assert improved quality from synthetic mocks, or promise a latency target without measurement.
- Existing graph/pipeline/ASR/translation/IfCondition/TTS regressions, asset loading and browser build must remain valid. Document errors, quotas, model cancellation, concurrent instances and any high-memory limitations.
- **The user's subjective evaluation of meeting-summary quality and the choice between the two models will happen after implementation; it is not a required pre-merge acceptance test.** Do not create an automatic "winner" or hardcode a default preference.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Both** named meeting-summary model Nodes appear in the extension Graph Editor, have equivalent primitive `TEXT` wiring and work independently with real local inference.
- [ ] Both support bounded incremental updates and coherent full-summary replace output, retaining decisions and unresolved issues while refusing to fabricate facts or owners when uncertain (validated with documented fixtures and examples).
- [ ] Model-specific pinned assets, legal notices, hardware requirements and packaged Worker runtimes are reviewed; per-model Save-time cache preparation, retry and no recording-time downloads function correctly.
- [ ] Real offline MV3 inference of **each** model is demonstrated, including a second update, Stop/Cancel lifecycle, saved/reloaded graphs, and output to a real Live display. Report exact test boundaries and failures.
- [ ] Existing graphs/defaults/independent branches work; appropriate unit/browser/extension build/tests and documentation are updated with results and explicit skips.
- [ ] The implementation is complete for both model options before closing this single Issue; user quality comparison remains out of scope.

## Required post-merge verification

None unless a true deployment-only requirement is discovered; record such verification distinctly as pending.

## Relevant code and model references

- `extension/graph.js`, `extension/graph-runtime.js`, `extension/graph-editor.js`, `extension/graph-model-preparation.js`, `extension/model-cache.js`, `extension/model-asset-cache.js`.
- `web/pipeline.js`, `web/text-nodes.js`, `web/correction-policy.js` and existing Worker / model cache integrations.
- Existing graph/window work: #115, #117, #119, #128. Product direction: #7.
- LFM ONNX: https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-JP-202606-ONNX
- Qwen ONNX: https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-ONNX-OPT
- Workflow: `docs/development-flow.md`, `docs/review-guidelines.md`.
